title: The Liquid Heist, an On-Chain Ransom & the Self-Custody Dip
subtitle: This week in Bitcoin & Nostr news

topics.title: Live Dashboard & Market
topics.description: Where Bitcoin sits live — and the money's answer to last week's dead-cat question

slides.heading: Live Dashboard
slides.body: Where Bitcoin sits right now. The full dashboards:

slides.heading: The Floor Answers (For Now)
slides.body: Last week's question: dead cat or real floor? This week the money answered.
bullets: September's day-one outflow reversed hard: ETFs took in $986.9M for the week ending Friday — the three-week total hit $3.8B, the strongest stretch of 2026
Thursday alone: roughly $731M in, the year's biggest single day. BlackRock's IBIT still takes about two-thirds of the flow
The test: Friday's ugly payrolls print knocked price briefly under $79K — and buyers took the dip against bad macro news
Scorecard: the bounce off $63K has now survived a September open AND a macro scare. That's floor behavior — same caveat as always: it's data, not destiny

topics.title: The Liquid Heist
topics.description: $320M walks out of the federation peg through a decade-old bugfix — then most of it walks back, negotiated entirely on-chain

slides.heading: The Liquid Heist: $320M Out of the Peg
slides.body: Saturday, about 4,000 BTC — roughly $320M — left Liquid's federation wallet. Not a key theft. A money printer.
bullets: The bug lived in Elements, Liquid's node software: an old 'fix' to range-proof caching glued two fields into the cache key with no separators. Stretch one field, shrink the other — same key, and an invalid proof sails through validation
So the attacker minted unbacked L-BTC and pegged it out for real BTC — via SideSwap's authorization key, which was never compromised. Neither was any federation key
mempool.space's mononaut traced it and delivered the line of the week: the most dangerous moment in a codebase is the commit that fixes something
orangesurf's ops finding stings too: no cap on a single peg-out, no daily limit — a nine-figure withdrawal got no manual review
Sidechain paused, bridge nodes off, exchanges froze L-BTC. Other Liquid assets unaffected

slides.heading: The Ransom, Settled On-Chain
slides.body: Then it got stranger: the negotiation happened in public, written into Bitcoin transactions.
bullets: PGP-signed messages embedded on-chain, opening with a flourish: 'You shall pay for your dereliction of duty'
Monday: 3,400 BTC came back to the federation. Kept: 598.5 BTC, about $47M — a self-awarded 'whitehat bounty' nobody agreed to
Sit with the mechanics: two parties who trust nothing about each other settled a nine-figure dispute on a public ledger. No court, no custodian, no phone call
Blockstream says the bug is patched and a coordinated federation restart is being prepared. The peg stays halted until it happens
The discussion question: what is a federated peg actually backed by? This week's answer — the code review

topics.title: The Self-Custody Dip
topics.description: River's report catches something that has never happened: coins leaving self-custody, on net

slides.heading: The Self-Custody Dip: First Decline in 15 Years
slides.body: River's new report caught a first: bitcoin held in self-custody went DOWN.
bullets: The stock is still enormous: about 13.83M BTC in individual self-custody — 65.9% of supply, roughly $1.09 trillion, triple the ETFs and treasuries combined
But the direction is new: the first net decline in about fifteen years of measurement
Who's moving: large holders swapping coins directly for ETF shares — in-kind, tax-efficient, no keys to manage. BlackRock's IBIT has absorbed $3B+ this way
Put it next to tonight's Liquid and Trezor stories: convenience keeps winning wallets back. Rooms like this one are the counter-argument

topics.title: Security Desk
topics.description: The Trezor breach quintuples on data that was 'deleted,' and Lightning merchants get two urgent patches

slides.heading: Security Desk: The Breach That Was 'Deleted'
slides.body: Trezor's shipping-partner breach got five times bigger this week — and the ugly part is why.
bullets: 67,000 more US customers exposed — orders from November 2019 to August 2021. August's disclosure said 13,689; same incident, now five times the size
What leaked: names, emails, phones, home addresses, order numbers. What didn't: seeds, keys, funds. The devices are fine
The kicker: ShipMonk gave Trezor written assurance that old data was deleted. It wasn't — attackers pulled it through a CVSS-10 hole in ShipMonk's analytics tool
The ShinyHunters extortion crew claims the hit. Translation: a list of hardware-wallet owners with home addresses is in circulation
Trezor's fix going forward is anonymized packaging. Yours is tonight's Quick Tip

slides.heading: Lightning Merchants: Patch Week, Again
slides.body: Two urgent updates for anyone running payments infrastructure.
bullets: BTCPay Server 2.4.4: a security release after attackers drained Lightning funds from unpatched merchants. Eight breaking changes — NFC payments off by default, zero-amount invoices blocked, API keys stored hashed. The maintainers' words: all server admins update
Alby Hub disclosed a critical flaw today: versions 1.7.0–1.18.5 with the management API reachable from the internet could be taken over — funds sent out. One known victim. Fix: v1.24.0
Both stories rhyme: the wallet cryptography held; the config and the perimeter didn't
If your node or store faces the internet, tonight's homework is two updates long

topics.title: Optech Corner
topics.description: #421: pools paying miners privately via silent payments, a Lightning ping-of-death, and the embargo clock runs out Thursday

slides.heading: Optech Corner: Private Payouts for Miners
slides.body: Newsletter #421's headline idea — pools paying miners without leaking every miner's finances.
bullets: Today's setup: pools pay hashers from a shared xpub. One database breach and every payout, past and future, is exposed
average_gary's proposal: BIP352 silent payments, right in the coinbase. The miner hands the pool one static address over Stratum v2's encrypted channel
The pool derives a fresh key per block — 34 bytes in the coinbase scriptSig — and the miner scans the chain for money only they can recognize
The theme: mining privacy is having a moment — Vinteum just ran a week-long mining-protocol deep dive in São Paulo, and the payout layer is catching up

slides.heading: The Ping of Death & the Embargo Clock
slides.body: Also in #421 — Lightning's disclosure culture keeps evolving.
bullets: Erick Cestari disclosed a Core Lightning denial-of-service: flood a node with pings demanding 65KB replies and never read the answers — buffers fill, the node crashes out of memory. No channel required
Fixed with backpressure in CLN's connect daemon; LND added its own ping rate-limits the same week. Upgrade line: CLN 25.09+, LND 0.21.3
And the callback from last week: CLN's sealed source from the embargo release unseals THURSDAY, September 11. Two weeks of binaries-first, then the code shows its work
Worth watching what precedent sticks: embargoed source may become the norm for money-adjacent bugs in the AI-report era

topics.title: Freedom Tech
topics.description: Peach's KYC-free pause gets its fine print — and the whitelist has zero names on it

slides.heading: Freedom Tech: Peach's Pause, in Numbers
slides.body: Last week: Swiss regulators requalified Peach's no-KYC escrow and the model paused. This week the fine print landed — and it's stricter than the headline.
bullets: To sell now you need one of three things: full identity verification, a manual whitelist approval, or a track record of 60+ trades with zero disputes
The whitelist currently has ZERO approved accounts. Buyers are capped at CHF 500 per trade with a 6% premium ceiling
What survives: the 2-of-2 multisig escrow Peach never could spend alone, the 2% fee, in-app dispute resolution — it stays non-custodial through the appeal
The stakes are bigger than one app: Switzerland is deciding whether NON-CUSTODIAL architecture counts as a regulatory defense at all
Read it next to Herat from last week: pressure lands on intermediaries. The peer-to-peer part nobody can requalify is still you, your keys, and a counterparty

topics.title: FIPS Watch
topics.description: v0.5.1 lands — the cleanup release that caps a fourteen-day sprint

slides.heading: FIPS Watch: v0.5.1 — The Cleanup Sprint
slides.body: Third release in two weeks. Refresher: FIPS is the mesh network where your Nostr key IS your network address.
bullets: v0.5.1 shipped Saturday: a maintenance release fixing the Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 packaging bug that kept the daemon from starting at all
Two discovery fixes teach the mesh better manners: a node no longer relays away the answer to its own lookup, and its own returning request no longer dings a peer's reputation
Wire-compatible with v0.5.0 — rolling upgrades, zero config changes
The cadence tells the story: armor (0.4.2) → reach (0.5.0) → polish (0.5.1), fourteen days end to end. Corgan is sprinting
Still pre-audit — same asterisk as every week

topics.title: Nostr This Week
topics.description: NostrMag picks a fight worth having: purity or growth — and Compass #39's ship list answers it

slides.heading: Nostr This Week: The 500,000-Purist Problem
slides.body: First, the argument of the week, via NostrMag: does Nostr want to stay pure, or get big?
bullets: The op-ed's claim: shunning bots, brands and celebrities caps Nostr at roughly 500K technical purists. Its blunt version: without corporations no ad revenue, without celebrities no mainstream pull
The proposed middle path: automation that declares itself (NIP-85), client-side filtering instead of relay censorship, and corporate npubs carrying their own trust scores
The counter-argument writes itself — we all watched ad-funded networks optimize for advertisers over users. Discussion question: which failure mode scares you more, small or sold?
Meanwhile the ecosystem shipped anyway: Block's Buzz and BitChat cracked GitHub's top-3 trending, and Damus Purple landed reliable large video uploads
And fuel for all of it: HRF's latest grant wave put 500M+ sats into 16 freedom-tech projects, Nostr development included

slides.heading: Compass #39: The Ship List
slides.body: Nostr Compass #39 landed this afternoon — while the philosophers argue, here's what shipped.
bullets: Git on Nostr grew up: GitWorkshop v3 and ngit put signed Git workflows on relays — now with PRIVATE repos, and ngit-ci 0.1: self-hosted CI whose results are themselves signed Nostr events. A whole forge, no GitHub
Shosho bridges your own Owncast stream to Nostr — discovery and chat ride the relays, the video stays on YOUR server. Self-hosted Twitch, purple-pilled
Plektos made gatherings fully private: guest list, RSVPs and threads encrypted together, invites that expire 30 days after the event. Meetup organizers, take note
cal.emre.xyz runs appointment scheduling on nothing but Nostr events (NIP-52) — availability and bookings live on relays, no database anywhere

And a security wave: Amber tightens signing-request attribution, ZapStore validates event ids and flags side-loaded packages, and LibreNostr's Orbot mode routes everything through Tor — and stops cold if Tor isn't there

topics.title: Builder Spotlight
topics.description: Mr.Hodl's EntropyLab — a whole hardware-wallet lab in one offline HTML file

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: EntropyLab
slides.body: Mr.Hodl built a hardware-wallet laboratory that fits in a single HTML file — and never touches the internet.
bullets: One file, opened offline: bring your own randomness — dice rolls, playing cards, any number — and it becomes a BIP-39 seed, with the fingerprint, xpubs and addresses to check it
The dice math matches COLDCARD, SeedSigner, Keystone and BitBox — same rolls, same seed. You can AUDIT your signer instead of trusting it
Under the hood it's rust-bitcoin compiled to WebAssembly; recent additions: BIP-85 child seeds, silent payments, PSBT editing, Taproot multisig, even a check for reused Schnorr nonces
Use it the way it's meant: download the file, run it air-gapped, wipe when done. It's a calculator, not a wallet — and it's labeled experimental, so treat it that way
Try it tonight: entropylab.online — or just scan the QR

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: You're on a list now — ship, talk, and click like it

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Ship Like You're Being Watched
slides.body: If you ordered a Trezor between 2019 and 2021 — or any hardware wallet, ever — assume your name and home address are on a list.
bullets: Never confirm you hold Bitcoin — not to callers, texters, or 'support.' The list proves a wallet was shipped; only YOU can confirm there's money behind it
Add a passphrase to your hardware wallet — a leaked address can find your door, not your extra word
Next device: ship to a PO box or pickup point, and use a nickname if the shop allows it
Read breach-season email skeptically: these lists power very convincing phishing. Trezor will never ask for your seed. Nobody legitimate will
